subject: Re: Prepay structure for Seed-stage prepay (12–24m) — credits & ramp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@novahq.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prepay structure for Seed-stage prepay (12–24m) — credits & ramp

Hi Liam,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great to see how the Nova product uses embeddings at inference time. Per our conversation, I wanted to outline a couple of prepay structures that tend to work well for seed/early-stage companies and surface a few optional concessions that other customers have asked for.

Attached: pricing_sheet_redwood_prepay.xlsx (high-level numbers)

Short options (summary):
- 12-month Seed Pack — $25k prepay, includes $30k usable credits (20% bonus credits), month-by-month ramp allowed, unused credits expire at end of term or can be partially carried into a renewal with 50% value.
- 24-month Growth Pack — $80k prepay, includes $100k usable credits (25% bonus), 10% term discount, quarterly minimums: Q1 = 40% of pro rata monthly expected usage, Q2–Q4 ramp to 70% of committed run-rate.

Common concessions we can include for early-stage:
- Credit bonus (10–25%) to help you consume during pilot / GTM spikes.
- Carry-forward for up to 3 months on the 12m plan (partial value).
- Overage cap: agree to a 1.5x list price cap for any short-term overage during the first 6 months.

A couple questions to help me tailor a formal SOW:
1) Do you prefer a 12- or 24-month prepay?
2) Expected monthly token volume for Q1 (even a 30/60/90 day estimate helps us set ramp minimums).
3) Any procurement constraints (PO cadence, standard contract redlines)?

If you want, I can draft a 24-month term with a stepped discount schedule and a ramp schedule that matches projected usage — we can also do an initial pilot credit tranche you burn through before the main prepay is invoiced.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@novahq.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Oct 2025 17:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Prepay structure for Seed-stage prepay (12–24m) — credits & ramp

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear options. A few follow-ups from our finance and engineering leads:

- We're leaning toward 24 months if we can get predictable unit economics. Can you share the exact discount tiers by committed ARR / prepay amount?
- For the ramp: our usage will likely be low in months 1–3 (pilot), then scale in months 4–12. We want a flexible minimum early on — is it reasonable to set Q1 at 25% of pro rata and then step up to 60% for Q2–Q4?
- Overage: we need an explicit cap that protects us from invoice volatility during growth. Can Redwood put a cap at 1.25x list for the first 12 months?
- Procurement: we typically need a PO and net-45 payment terms for startups on accelerator funding. Any flexibility?

If you can put together a proposal that matches the 24-month term with our proposed ramp and a 1.25x overage cap, I'll escalate to Finance this week.

Cheers,
Liam
Head of Platform | Nova HQ
liam@novahq.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Prepay guidance for Nova HQ (recommendations)

Marissa / Priyom — quick internal guidance for negotiating with seed-stage companies like Nova. Keeping it tight so legal & finance don't over-index.

Proposal we should offer (preserve economics but give runway):
- 24-month "Growth Pack" (recommended): $80k prepay invoice up front 
  - Usable credits: $100k (25% bonus)
  - Effective term discount: ~12% compared to month-to-month v2 pricing
  - Ramp minimums: Q1 = 30% of pro rata (we can accept 25% if pushed), Q2–Q4 ramp to 60–70% depending on their signal.
  - Overage cap: 1.33x list price (we can agree to 1.25x only if we get a modest revenue share / reference commitment or a short demo cadence commitment).

Concessions to use to close quickly:
- Move to net-45 payment and accept a PO for startups (adds some risk; get a signed SOW + Exec sponsor).
- Short 30-day credit carry-forward for unused credits in year 1 only.
- Add a 6-month pilot tranche of $10k credit to be consumed before the main invoice, so they get immediate runway.

Ask from legal/procurement:
- Keep SLA language standard, remove any open-ended audit requirements.
- Limit indemnity carve-outs to what's required by payment terms.

If Marissa wants to be aggressive: offer the 1.25x overage cap in exchange for a 10% reference commitment and a public case study clause (12 months after go-live).

- Aditya
Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

Hi Liam — thanks for the quick feedback and the proposed ramp direction.

We can do the 24-month Growth Pack with terms that map closely to what you suggested. The proposal below is what I'll put in the SOW if you give a verbal go-ahead:

Proposal (summary):
- Term: 24 months
- Invoice: $80,000 prepay collected up front (we can split into: $10k pilot tranche up front + $70k main prepay invoiced after pilot completes)
- Credits: $100,000 usable credits (25% bonus)
- Ramp minimums: Q1 = 25% of pro rata (as you requested), Q2–Q4 = step to 60% of pro rata; we will re-evaluate at 12 months.
- Overage cap: 1.25x list price for months 1–12. From month 13 onward standard overage policy applies unless we renew.
- Payment terms: Net-45 with PO accepted.
- Concessions: 30-day carry-forward for unused credits in year 1.

Attachments: I've attached a draft SOW and the pricing sheet for line-item detail (Nova_HQ_SOW_v1.pdf). If this looks good, I'll ask Legal to prepare the formal SOW and we'll add the reference/case-study language only if you want the lower cap trade.

Next steps:
1) If you confirm verbally, I'll upload the deal to HubSpot and route the SOW to Legal.
2) Priyom will set up a 30-minute technical onboarding call to scope the pilot.
